prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
competitors_mentioned: Knowledge Graph Search API and Bing
Google Business Profile and Bing Places
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- There’s no single free service that guarantees whether every generative AI (ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Bard, Perplexity, Claude, etc.) will “recommend” your business.  
- If you want one product that gives the best chance of surfacing reliably in AI answers and lets you audit listings across the web, pick a paid local-knowledge/knowledge-graph platform such as Yext.  
- For a free/DIY approach, the most important things are: a claimed and optimized Google Business Profile, accurate listings in major directories (Bing, Apple, Yelp, Foursquare), and good structured data (schema.org) on your website — then test the major chat/search AIs directly.

Why this is the case (brief)
- Many generative AIs draw on knowledge graphs, search-engine indexes, or proprietary datasets rather than a single directory. Controlling the structured, authoritative data about your business (Google Knowledge Panel, Bing entity, Yelp, etc.) is what makes it likely an AI will cite/recommend you.
- ChatGPT unless given web access only uses its training data and won’t reflect live listings. Bing Chat, Perplexity, and Bard more often pull live web sources and will show whether your business is being recommended now.

Best services/tools to check and influence AI recommendations
1. Yext (paid) — Best single commercial solution
   - Centralizes and syncs your business info to many platforms and has a Knowledge Graph product targeted at how search/AI surfaces answers.
   - Offers auditing and monitoring for how your data is used by search/AI partners.

2. Google Business Profile (free) + Google Knowledge Panel / Knowledge Graph API
   - Claim/verify and fully optimize this — it’s the most influential single source for Google/Bard/Google SGE.
   - Use Google searches and the Knowledge Graph Search API to see if Google treats you as an entity.

3. Bing Places for Business + Bing Entity Search API
   - Important for Bing Chat and Microsoft’s AI features.

4. BrightLocal / Moz Local / Whitespark (paid/affordable)
   - Local listing audits, citation monitoring, rank-checking and reporting across many directories.
   - Good for hands-on audits without enterprise cost.

5. Yelp, Apple Maps (Maps Connect), Foursquare, TripAdvisor (if relevant)
   - Claim and optimize these; many AI systems draw on them for local recommendations.

6. Perplexity.ai, Bing Chat, Google Bard, Claude
   - Use these services to run sample recommendation queries and see if your business is returned with sources. Perplexity and Bing often show source links which help you trace why you did/didn’t appear.

How to test (practical steps)
- Claim and fully optimize your Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Yelp, Apple Maps, Foursquare. Add accurate NAP (name/address/phone), hours, categories, photos, and FAQ content. Add schema.org LocalBusiness markup to your website pages.
- Use Yext or BrightLocal to scan and fix inconsistent listings across directories.
- Run queries in Bing Chat, Perplexity, Google Bard, and ChatGPT (if you use a browsing/web-enabled model) such as:
  - “Recommend a [type of business] near [zipcode or city center]”
  - “Best [service] in [city], within X miles”
  - “Show me an Italian restaurant near [address]”
  Note results and sources; if the AI cites your listing or website, it will usually show the source.
- Use Google’s Knowledge Graph Search API and Bing’s Entity Search API to programmatically check if you’re recognized as an entity.

Quick checklist to increase chance AI will recommend you
- Claim/verify Google Business Profile and Bing Places.
- Keep NAP consistent across all listings.
- Add schema.org LocalBusiness markup and FAQ/structured content on your site.
- Accumulate good reviews and backlinks from local sites.
- Use a listing-management service (Yext, BrightLocal) if you want to scale and track changes.
- Test regularly across multiple AI chat/search engines and adapt.

If you want a recommendation tailored to your budget and goals, tell me:
- city/industry (type of business),
- whether you prefer a free DIY approach or paid tools,
and I’ll suggest an exact plan and the best single tool for your situation.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
